items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: our St. Mary’s band, Frasier Scott, one of our trombonists and I, we went out for a beer on intermission.

ctx.x: Yeah. I experienced that. That’s not just hearsay. That was my experience. And another experience, during World War II I was playing at the Stage Door Canteen, our St. Mary’s band, Frasier Scott, one of our trombonists and I, we went out for a beer on intermission. And we went to this little, it was patterned after a cable car, a little bar, to get a beer on intermission. And in our uniforms, the uniform of our country, the bartender said, “If you want a drink you’ll have to go out in the Fillmore.” I said, “Well…

in this town — I guess maybe after the gold rush, or I don’t know when the color bar maybe got to be broader. But I can remember my experiences, even as a kid, they opened a miniature golf course on Fillmore and Sutter, right into Fillmore, right in the middle of the Western Addition, where most of the people lived. Miniature golf. And they wouldn’t sell tickets to colored.
